reader.decision: Approve passing `conn` into `hold_seats`, on the condition that Aelita first checks for every other caller of `hold_seats` and updates or reports them before merging.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows a nested pool acquisition: 10 requests each hold a connection and wait for a second one. That fills the pool of 10 while Postgres sits at 38 of 200. Using one connection per request removes the cause. Raising `max_size` only moves the threshold. The one open risk is other callers of `hold_seats`, which the fix would break.

reconstruction.problem: `checkout` takes a pool connection at `app/checkout.py:6`. It then calls `hold_seats`, which asks the same pool (max_size=10) for a second connection at `app/seats.py:5`. Under the on-sale burst, 10 requests hold all connections and each waits for another, so the pool deadlocks.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Checkout froze for 30 seconds until `timeout=30` expired. Then 10 `PoolTimeout` errors in `hold_seats` and 4 in `checkout` produced 14 `500` responses at once, and the next wave failed the same way at 19:01:02. Postgres was idle at 38 of 200 connections. At normal traffic (`in_flight` 3 or below) it never shows. A second bug: the seat hold commits on its own connection, so a failure after line 12 rolls back the order but leaves the seats held for 10 minutes.
reconstruction.fix: Change `hold_seats(event_id, seat_ids)` to `hold_seats(conn, event_id, seat_ids)` and run the `UPDATE` on the passed connection. Delete the `pool` import in `app/seats.py`. Change the call at `app/checkout.py:12` to pass `conn`. Each request then uses one connection and one transaction. The alternative is raising `max_size`, which only moves the threshold and multiplies connections across 4 pods against `max_connections=200`.
reconstruction.cost: The transaction stays open slightly longer because the seat `UPDATE` now runs inside the order transaction. Any other caller of `hold_seats` breaks and has not been checked yet.

follow_up_questions: Which other callers of `hold_seats` exist, if any, and what will change in each?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve passing `conn` into `hold_seats` so each checkout uses one connection and one transaction. Search for other callers of `hold_seats` first and update them in the same change.
